messages:
mira: Heads up — saw weird kernel picks in perf logs for r3 models on A100-80GB in prod. Uploaded trace: https://redwood-internal/trace/abc123. We need consistent telemetry fields for WHY a kernel was chosen (hw, seq_len, quant, fallback) and a compact reason enum.

 dan: Agree. Current logs only show kernel id and latency, not the decision reason. Proposed fields: kernel, reason_code, seq_len_bucket, batch, hw_arch, sm, quant_support, kv_cache_hit, env_flags. Also include selected_alt_kernel when fallback occurs.

 josh: Quick patch I tried locally: added env REDWOOD_KERNEL_DECISION=1 and print 'decision=...'. sample line from my run:

```
[KERNEL_DECISION] kernel=gpt_conv_v2 reason=seq_threshold seq=1024 batch=1 hw=A100 sm=80 quant=none kv_hit=false latency_ms=18.2
```

It surfaces the decision path.

 sarah: This is useful, but two concerns: noise volume and privacy. We must NOT log full model weights/ids or prompt text. Keep it to model family + version tag if needed. Also compress reason to short enums: seq_thresh, arch_match, quant_pref, cache_hit, fallback_cap, profile_override.

 alvaro: Another real-world gotcha — the batcher sometimes coalesces short and long sequences and we end up on a different kernel due to padding. Add batch_pad_ratio and batch_type (homogeneous/mixed) to help debug. Also track kv_cache_behavior (prefetch, hit_ratio) since cache hits influence seq path.

 dan: Also propose a short debug mode: REDWOOD_KERNEL_DEBUG_SAMPLER=<duration>. When enabled, emit verbose decision dump for a sampled fraction of requests or for a time window (e.g., 30s) with request_id so we can correlate. Default off.

 mira: Good. Let's make two outputs: 1) one-line structured entry per request intended for metrics/log pipeline (low-cardinality fields) and 2) an optional verbose dump (multi-line) gated by the sampler flag. Metric fields should be tagged for aggregation: kernel_choice:reason, kernel_choice:arch, kernel_choice:seq_bucket.

 deploy-bot: deploy-bot: patch/eng-runtime/kernel-decision-telemetry -> staging applied. Logs will appear under /var/log/redwood/kernel_decision.log and be forwarded to ingest-kafka/topic=kernel-decisions (staging).

 josh: Proposed single-line JSON for ingestion (example):

```
{"kernel":"gpt_conv_v2","reason":"seq_thresh","seq_len":"1024","seq_bucket":"1k-2k","batch":1,"batch_type":"homogeneous","batch_pad_ratio":"0.05","arch":"a100","sm":"80","quant":"none","kv_hit":"false","lat_ms":"18.2","env_flags":"REDWOOD_KERNEL_DECISION=1","timestamp":"2026-02-25T16:53:04Z","request_id":"req-12ab"}
```

 Note: the top-level ingestion JSON is acceptable because it's a string payload to the pipeline; we will avoid logging prompt/model input.

 sarah: For privacy/compliance: add a scrubber in the logger that asserts model_name in allowed list and replaces unknown values with 'redacted_model'. Also limit rate of verbose dumps to avoid PII leakage.

 dan: Action items: josh to open PR with the env flags + one-line JSON format + unit tests for scrubber; I'll add metric tags in the router; mira will coordinate a short staging run and a perf baseline.

 mira: Thanks — let's keep the sampling conservative initially. If anyone sees a regressions spike when enabling this in staging, drop the sampler immediately.

 josh: FYI sample CLI for debug: export REDWOOD_KERNEL_DECISION=1; export REDWOOD_KERNEL_DEBUG_SAMPLER=30s; ./serve --route r3-tests

 deploy-bot: deploy-bot: staging collection enabled.

 mira: Closing loop — we'll reconvene after the staging run. If the telemetry looks good we can add an opt-in for dedicated customers.
